findings.message: Unrequested behavior change: NO_COLOR was changed from `"NO_COLOR" in os.environ` to `os.getenv("NO_COLOR")`. With the old code, `NO_COLOR=""` disabled color; now an empty value no longer disables it, so a documented behavior silently changes. docs/resources/troubleshooting.rst:146 states Loguru "disables coloring if it is set to any value", which is now false; that page and the |the-no-color-environment-variable| reference were not updated. The change is defensible per no-color.org (which ignores an empty value), but it is out of scope for this FORCE_COLOR issue and is a regression against the previously documented contract.
findings.suggestion: Either keep `"NO_COLOR" in os.environ` to preserve existing behavior, or, if intentionally aligning with the spec, update docs/resources/troubleshooting.rst:146 to say the variable disables color only when set to a non-empty value, and add a test for the `NO_COLOR=""` case.

findings.message: The new FORCE_COLOR feature has no test coverage. tests/test_colorama.py and tests/test_add_option_colorize.py contain tests for NO_COLOR/PYCHARM/CI/TERM but nothing exercises FORCE_COLOR (grep for FORCE_COLOR matches only the implementation). There is also no CHANGELOG.rst entry, while the sibling NO_COLOR feature is documented there (CHANGELOG.rst:9). Without a test, the intended precedence (NO_COLOR over FORCE_COLOR), the empty-string case, and the non-tty forcing path are unverified.
findings.suggestion: Add tests analogous to test_honor_no_color_standard, e.g. parametrized over patched streams asserting should_colorize(StreamIsattyFalse()) is True when FORCE_COLOR="1", False when FORCE_COLOR="", and False when both NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR are set. Add a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

findings.message: `os.getenv("FORCE_COLOR")` treats any non-empty value as truthy, so FORCE_COLOR="0" (or "false") forces color. This matches the literal force-color.org spec ("regardless of its value"), but diverges from ecosystems that treat "0"/"false" as disabling (Node/chalk). Worth a conscious decision and a comment noting the rationale so it isn't mistaken for a bug later.
findings.suggestion: If spec-literal semantics are intended, keep as-is but document it (docs troubleshooting section + code comment). Otherwise special-case falsy-looking values. Not required for correctness against force-color.org.
